newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Solzhenitsyn hospitalised with heart condition.
newsitem.headline: Solzhenitsyn hospitalised with heart condition.

text.p: Russian writer Alexander Solzhenitsyn, who fought the Soviet Union before turning his fire on capitalist Russia, has been taken to hospital with a heart condition, his secretary said on Wednesday.
"He feels all right and did not have a heart attack," Munira Urazova told Reuters by telephone.
The 79-year-old Nobel Prize winner was admitted to the Central Clinical Hospital on May 12 with heart problems, Uradova said, but did not specify what was wrong with him.
The hospital confirmed Solzhenitsyn was there and said there was "nothing serious" wrong with the author. "He is all right," a doctor said.
Solzhenitsyn won the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1970 for writings which publicised the harshness of the Soviet prison camp system, in which he spent nearly a decade.
Expelled from the Soviet Union in 1974, Solzhenitsyn lived in exile in rural America for 20 years before returning to Russia where he blasted its new leaders for being just as bad as the communists.
The author of "A day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich", "First Circle" and "Cancer Ward" has led a discreet life since his weekly television programme was taken off the air in 1995.

The bearded firebrand, who says his country has lost its spiritual roots and favours a kind of 19th century rural nationalism, was widely criticised for being out of touch with modern Russia after his long exile abroad.
